newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Croats, Moslems hold assembly without Serbs.
newsitem.headline: Croats, Moslems hold assembly without Serbs.

text.p: Croat and Moslem deputies inaugurated Bosnia's new inter-ethnic parliament on Saturday despite the refusal of Serb legislators to attend.
Croat and Moslem members of the House of Representatives elected last month stood on the stage of Sarajevo's national theatre and signed an oath of office.
Duncan Bullivant, a spokesman for the international High Representative in Bosnia, said that the inauguration of the new collective presidency, also due on Saturday, had been postponed.
"We will go ahead with the first session of the House of Representatives but the Serbs are definitely not coming," Bullivant told reporters.
Momcilo Krajisnik, the Serb member of the three-man presidency, told mediators the Serbs could not accept the venue for the ceremony or the text of a proposed oath of loyalty to Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Bullivant called the Serb stance "puerile and ridiculous".
